coverage.assessment: Cutting the 'conspired towards an education' sentence leaves 'this problem' without an antecedent. The boys' assumption that churches would always go on was also cut, which thins the 'Presidents nor Churches' payoff. The State Street, Cunard, and silence setups survive.

Without 'on his way to Washington,' the President is last seen as an invalid at Mount Vernon Street and then falls 'on the floor of the House.' The reader cannot reconcile the two falls. The revision improved other referents, notably the President bringing up the peaches and Mr. Everett at the eulogy.
The gardener's single line is preserved exactly, with its attribution and its effect on the boy.

The first draft stopped the Abigail sentence at 'Abigail was right,' turning the source's qualified irony into a plain endorsement. Other qualifiers survive: 'Probably' on Polk, 'could never make up his mind,' 'seven at the utmost,' and 'close on eighty.'
The narration keeps the boy's limited view under the old man's retrospect. The great-grandfather remains known only as an idea tied to Quincy. Nothing is revealed prematurely.

The first draft lost the mock-political vocabulary after the walk ('tool of tyranny,' 'social compact'). The revision introduced a stray comma ('every Adams, had lived'). Double hyphens, aphorisms, and the dash-built lists are otherwise intact.

The Madam's 'cross in life… to the boy it was her charm' was cut, weakening the boy's attraction to the un-Bostonian side that his 'half exotic' inheritance relies on. Cutting the grandfathers paragraph is legitimate because paragraph 13 already carries the equal-kindness point.
All six local endpoints survive, as do the partner endpoints in 034, 031, 037, 018, and 005. Partner 001 is omitted, but 031 carries the multiplicity title.

strengths: The school walk is preserved in full sequence: the guest-mother disadvantage, the silent descent, the escape reasoning, the turned 'strategical points,' the Polk speculation, and the 'stoniest soil' close.
All eight verbatim passages survive exactly, including the closing State Street cadence.
The revision clarified referents the first draft had left vague: 'which the President brought up,' 'How could Mr. Everett say there,' and naming 'Louisa Catherine' before 'Louisa.'

Cutting the separate grandfathers paragraph is a clean removal, because paragraph 13 already states that the Brooks grandfather was 'equally kind' and that the preference came only from country and summer.
The sense catalogue keeps the full smell list and 'the taste of A-B, AB,' and the double hyphens are preserved.
summary: The revision keeps all eight verbatim passages, every essential beat, and an intact school-walk sequence. It also fixes several referents: 'the President brought up,' 'Mr. Everett,' and the naming of 'Louisa Catherine.' Its new cuts, however, create two coherence breaks. 'This problem' now has no antecedent. Dropping 'on his way to Washington' leaves the Mount Vernon Street fall and the House fall unreconciled. Smaller revision cuts weaken the Madam's charm for the boy, the church premise, and one sentence's grammar. The first draft had already flattened the Abigail irony and the mock-political irony after the walk. The revision runs shorter than the first draft, so the small restorations below fit the budget.
